checks.name: FV3: comparison where the map overlaps the square
checks.note: Not applicable. No point of the Jamaica Bay map lies in the square (0 of 109,875); the map's cells cover 0 m² of it; the nearest point is 2,046 m from the square.
checks.rule: compare depths only where the map overlaps; below 1% of the square [P] the result is 'not applicable'

checks.name: FV5: who saw the flood (reported, not judged)
checks.rule: for each storm, counts inside the square from Groundsource, Storm Events, 311, FloodNet and the surveyed marks, each by its stated rule; 311 over the storm days and the 1 day after (CH-24)

checks.name: FV5: the two 311 fetches agree on the storm days
checks.rule: rows, requests and twin pairs in the square on the storm days are the same in the storm-day fetch and in the fetch of the weeks round the storm, which the main counts read (CH-24)

checks.name: FV5: 311 counts both naming schemes
checks.note: Reported. The facts row says 'count both'; on 29 Sep 2023 most rows of the current scheme have a twin of the legacy scheme, so counting rows would count most requests twice.
checks.rule: rows of the legacy and the current scheme are both read; rows of one request under both schemes are paired (nyc_311.twins, the strict case of observations.sightings) and counted once

checks.name: FV5: reports of the same flooding combined into sightings
checks.note: Reported, not judged. Rule accepted in CH-24 (2026-11-27); the limits stay placeholders, to be re-tested in F8 on more storms. The sensitivity table (tables.sightings_sensitivity) gives the count for other thresholds; tables.storm_days_only the counts on the storm days alone.
checks.rule: observations of 311, FloodNet and the marks within 50 m [P] and 12 h [P] of each other, chained, are one sighting; every member kept (observations.sightings); over the 311 window (CH-24)

checks.name: FV5: late calls, the day after the storm against dry days
checks.note: Reported. Ida's day after is clearly above the baseline; on this evidence CH-24 (accepted 2026-11-27) extends every storm's 311 window by 1 day after the storm, for both storms as one rule.
checks.rule: requests on the day after the storm above every dry baseline day and at least 2 times the baseline mean [P]

notes: F5 second part (FV3, FV5). Counts are reported, not judged. Not applicable. No point of the Jamaica Bay map lies in the square (0 of 109,875); the map's cells cover 0 m² of it; the nearest point is 2,046 m from the square.
Storm Events clock: every New York City row says EST-5; times are turned into UTC and then into the New York wall clock before a day is matched (facts noaa-storm-events, time_zone).
311: created_date has no zone; read as the New York wall clock as written.

Sightings (observations.sightings) are the lab's grouping, refining the facts row's 'count both': twin rows are one request, and reports close in place and time are one sighting with every member kept. Change CH-24, accepted by Yuri on 2026-11-27: the rule as stated, its limits placeholders [P] to be re-tested in F8, and each storm's 311 window extended by 1 day after the storm; the main counts, sightings and maps use that window, tables.storm_days_only keeps the storm days alone.

who_saw_counts.png: Counts inside the model square for each source and storm. Dark bar: the main count (Groundsource places centred in the square; Storm Events flood events with a point in it; 311 flooding-related requests with twin rows of the two naming schemes paired; FloodNet sensors that recorded an event; USGS marks). Light bar: the context (places touching the square; flood events of the square's counties and zones; 311 rows of both schemes; sensors in service; mark sites). Windows: Ida 1 and 2 Sep 2021, the other storm 29 Sep 2023, each source by its own date rule (record, RULES); 311 also takes the day after each storm (CH-24: 1-3 Sep 2021, 29-30 Sep 2023). Counts are reported, not judged: a source with no entry is not evidence of no flood.

who_saw_map_ida_2021.png: Ida, 1-2 Sep 2021 (311 and sightings: 1-3 Sep 2021, CH-24): who saw the flood inside the model square. Background: the frozen F3 replay of this storm, maximum inundation depth from 0.05 m (for orientation only; nothing is compared). Purple dots: 311 flooding-related requests, a twin pair drawn once. Black rings: sightings of more than one report (observations.sightings: within 50 m and 12 h, chained), the number of reports beside rings of three or more. Green squares: FloodNet sensors in service (filled: recorded an event). Black diamonds: USGS marks. Orange outlines: Groundsource places of the storm days, solid when centred in the square, dashed when within 500 m and no larger than the square (larger places, such as a borough, are counted but not drawn). Dotted red: the hull of the points of a Storm Events event with a point in the square.

floodnet.inside: the sensor table's position, projected to EPSG:32618, lies in the square
floodnet.window: context: sensors in service on a storm day (installed on or before it, not removed before it); main count: sensors with an event whose start (GMT) falls on a storm day on the New York clock

groundsource.inside: main count: the place polygon's centroid lies in the square; context: the polygon intersects the square (the polygon is the named place, not the flood)
groundsource.window: a row whose start_date to end_date range (as published: days, no time of day, no zone) holds one of the storm's days

nyc_311.inside: latitude and longitude, projected to EPSG:32618, fall in the square; requests with no location cannot be placed and are counted apart for the two boroughs (on the storm days only: the fetch of the weeks round the storm holds placed rows only)
nyc_311.window: created_date (a floating time stamp, read as the New York wall clock as written) falls in the storm's 311 window: the storm days and the 1 day after (CH-24; Ida 1-3 Sep 2021, 2023 29-30 Sep 2023). Rows from the fetch of the weeks round the storm (flooding types only); the storm-day fetch gives the same rows on the storm days

storm_events.inside: main count: the begin point, end point or a point of the locations file lies in the square; context: every flood event of the square's counties (Kings, New York) and NWS zones (75 Kings (Brooklyn), 72 New York (Manhattan)), county and zone events both read
storm_events.window: the event's begin to end, turned from its CZ_TIMEZONE clock (EST-5 for every New York City row, also in September) to UTC and then to the New York wall clock, holds one of the storm's days

usgs_marks.inside: the mark's position, projected to EPSG:32618, lies in the square
usgs_marks.window: the survey of Ida (ScienceBase item 618975c8d34ec04fc9c5a049); no date matching. The cache holds no survey for 29 Sep 2023; whether USGS surveyed marks for that storm was not checked

sighting_rule.area_reports: Groundsource places (centred in the square) and Storm Events events (with a point in the square) name an area, not a spot: they join no sighting and link none; each sighting lists the area reports whose shape holds a member (Groundsource: the place polygon over the storm days; Storm Events: the hull of the event's points over its begin to end), with windows within 12 h
sighting_rule.duplicates: the strict case, applied first: 311 twin rows of one request (nyc_311.twins = sightings.duplicate_pairs: other scheme, same kind, within 600 s, same address or within 25 m)
sighting_rule.near: two observations within 50 m [P] and with time windows within 12 h [P] of each other; any source, any kind
sighting_rule.observation: one report of water at a place and time, over the storm's 311 window (the storm days and the day after, CH-24): 311 requests (a twin pair is one observation keeping both row ids; time = created_date), FloodNet events at sensors in the square that started in the window (time = start to end, New York clock), USGS marks in the square (no time: the whole window)
sighting_rule.sighting: observations joined by chains of near pairs (single linkage); every member is kept with its source and row ids; extent = largest distance between two members
